  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>

    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The equation that describes the velocity of a uniform accelerated body v = v0 + a*t is a functional icon. In general every analitical solution of a mathematical model can be considered an icon. A functional icon expresses its similarity with the object when is part of a process the makes it imitate the behavior of the object. In the case of v = v0 + a*t, plotting the velocity over time or listing their values at certain instants is when the icon expresses it functionality.</td>

ConventionalProperty
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_d8aa8e1f_b650_416d_88a0_5118de945456">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_d8aa8e1f_b650_416d_88a0_5118de945456</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A property that is associated to an object by convention, or assumption.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">ConventionalProperty</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A quantitative property attributed by agreement to a quantity for a given purpose.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The thermal conductivity of a copper sample in my laboratory can be assumed to be the conductivity that appears in the vendor specification. This value has been obtained by measurement of a sample which is not the one I have in my laboratory. This conductivity value is then a conventional quantitiative property assigned to my sample through a semiotic process in which no actual measurement is done by my laboratory.<br><br>If I don&#x27;t believe the vendor, then I can measure the actual thermal conductivity. I then perform a measurement process that semiotically assign another value for the conductivity, which is a measured property, since is part of a measurement process.<br><br>Then I have two different physical quantities that are properties thanks to two different semiotic processes.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_dd4a7f3e_ef56_466c_ac1a_d2716b5f87ec">ObjectiveProperty</a></td>
  </tr>
  </table>

DimensionalUnit
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_cbdea88b_fef1_4c7c_b69f_ae1f0f241c4a">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_cbdea88b_fef1_4c7c_b69f_ae1f0f241c4a</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The current version of EMMO does not provide explicit classes for physical dimensions. Rather it embraces the fact that the physical dimensionality of a physical quantity is carried by its measurement unit.<br><br>The role of dimensional unit and its subclasses is to express the physical dimensionality that is carried by the unit.<br><br>Since the dimensionality of a physical quantity can be written as the product of powers of the physical dimensions of the base quantities in the selected system of quantities, the physical dimensionality of a measurement unit is uniquely determined by the exponents. For a dimensional unit, at least one of these exponents must be non-zero (making it disjoint from dimensionless units).</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">DimensionalUnit</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A subclass of measurement unit focusing on the physical dimensionality that is carried by the unit.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>

MetrologicalUncertainty
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_847724b7_acef_490e_9f0d_67da967f2812">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_847724b7_acef_490e_9f0d_67da967f2812</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Metrological uncertainty in EMMO is a slight generalisation of the VIM term &#x27;measurement uncertainty&#x27;, which is defined as &quot;a non-negative parameter characterising the dispersion of the quantity being measured&quot;.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">In general, for a given set of information, it is understood that the measurement uncertainty is associated with a stated quantity value. A modification of this value results in a modification of the associated uncertainty.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Metrological uncertainty includes components arising from systematic effects, such as components associated with corrections and the assigned quantity values of measurement standards, as well as the definitional uncertainty. Sometimes estimated systematic effects are not corrected for but, instead, associated measurement uncertainty components are incorporated.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A metrological uncertainty can be assigned to any objective property via the &#x27;hasMetrologicalUncertainty&#x27; relation.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">MetrologicalUncertainty</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The uncertainty of a quantity obtained through a well-defined procedure, characterising of the dispersion of the quantity.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">- Standard deviation<br>- Half-width of an interval with a stated coverage probability</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_dd4a7f3e_ef56_466c_ac1a_d2716b5f87ec">ObjectiveProperty</a></td>
  </tr>

    <td class="element-table-value">&quot;Ordinal quantities, such as Rockwell C hardness, are usually not considered to be part of a system of quantities because they are related to other quantities through empirical relations only.&quot;<br>International vocabulary of metrology (VIM)</td>

PhysicalQuantity
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_02c0621e_a527_4790_8a0f_2bb51973c819">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_02c0621e_a527_4790_8a0f_2bb51973c819</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">In the same system of quantities, dim ρB = ML−3 is the quantity dimension of mass concentration of component B, and ML−3 is also the quantity dimension of mass density, ρ.<br>ISO 80000-1</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Measured or simulated &#x27;physical propertiy&#x27;-s are always defined by a physical law, connected to a physical entity through a model perspective and measurement is done according to the same model.<br><br>Systems of units suggests that this is the correct approach, since except for the fundamental units (length, time, charge) every other unit is derived by mathematical relations between these fundamental units, implying a physical laws or definitions.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Measurement units of quantities of the same quantity dimension may be designated by the same name and symbol even when the quantities are not of the same kind.<br><br>For example, joule per kelvin and J/K are respectively the name and symbol of both a measurement unit of heat capacity and a measurement unit of entropy, which are generally not considered to be quantities of the same kind.<br><br>However, in some cases special measurement unit names are restricted to be used with quantities of specific kind only.<br><br>For example, the measurement unit ‘second to the power minus one’ (1/s) is called hertz (Hz) when used for frequencies and becquerel (Bq) when used for activities of radionuclides.<br><br>As another example, the joule (J) is used as a unit of energy, but never as a unit of moment of force, i.e. the newton metre (N · m).</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">— quantities of the same kind have the same quantity dimension,<br>— quantities of different quantity dimensions are always of different kinds, and<br>— quantities having the same quantity dimension are not necessarily of the same kind.<br>ISO 80000-1</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">PhysicalQuantity</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A &#x27;Mathematical&#x27; entity that is made of a &#x27;Numeral&#x27; and a &#x27;MeasurementUnit&#x27; defined by a physical law, connected to a physical entity through a model perspective. Measurement is done according to the same model.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#Thing">Thing</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_67fc0a36_8dcb_4ffa_9a43_31074efa3296">hasMetrologicalReference</a> only <a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_b081b346_7279_46ef_9a3d_2c088fcd79f4">MeasurementUnit</a></td>

Quantity
^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_0650c031_42b6_4f0a_b62d_d88f071da6bf">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_0650c031_42b6_4f0a_b62d_d88f071da6bf</a></td>

  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">VIM defines a quantity as a &quot;property of a phenomenon, body, or substance, where the property has a magnitude that can be expressed as a number and a reference&quot;.<br><br>A quantity in EMMO is a property and therefore only addresses the first part of the VIM definition (that is a property of a phenomenon, body, or substance). The second part (that it can be expressed as a number and a reference) is syntactic and addressed by emmo:QuantityValue.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>

QuantityValue
^^^^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_f658c301_ce93_46cf_9639_4eace2c5d1d5">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_f658c301_ce93_46cf_9639_4eace2c5d1d5</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A quantity value is not necessarily a property, since it is possible to write &quot;10 kg&quot;, without assigning this quantity to a specific object.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Following the International Vocabulary of Metrology (VIM), EMMO distinguishes between a quantity (a property) and the quantity value (a numerical and a reference).<br><br>So, for the EMMO the symbol &quot;kg&quot; is not a physical quantity but simply a &#x27;Symbolic&#x27; object categorized as a &#x27;MeasurementUnit&#x27;.<br><br>While the string &quot;1 kg&quot; is a &#x27;QuantityValue&#x27;.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">QuantityValue</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A symbolic that has parts a numerical object and a reference expressing the value of a quantity (expressed as the product of the numerical and the unit).</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">6.8 m<br>0.9 km<br>8 K<br>6 MeV<br>43.5 HRC(150 kg)</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Vimterm</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">quantity value</td>
  </tr>

    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>

Ablation
^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_1a2cbca8_3d3b_4e2c_9a71_e39273937786">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_1a2cbca8_3d3b_4e2c_9a71_e39273937786</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Manufacturing by separating particles of material from a solid body by non-mechanical means. Ablation refers both to the removal of layers of material and to the separation of workpiece parts. The production process of ablation is considered in its stationary instantaneous state, independently of the application of auxiliary processes necessary to initiate the process. Ablation is divided into three subgroups according to the order point of view (OGP) &quot;process in the effective zone on the surface of the workpiece&quot;: - thermal ablation; - chemical ablation; - electrochemical ablation.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>

^^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Free forming is pressure forming with tools that do not or only partially contain the shape of the workpiece and move against each other.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Non la metterei</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Printing forms with tools that do not or only partially contain the shape of the workpiece and move against each other. The workpiece shape is created by free or fixed relative movement between the tool and the workpiece (kinematic shape generation).</td>
  </tr>

  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>

  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Deals with entities that have a undefined shape. Undefined means that the actual shape of the entity that is produced is not relevant for the definition of the process.<br>In fact, everything has a shape, but in process engineering this is not relevant.<br><br>e.g. the fact that steel comes in sheets is not relevant for the definition of steel material generated in a steel-making process.</td>

    <td class="element-table-value">This concepts encompass the overall lifetime of a product.<br>Is temporaly fundamental, meaning that it can have other products as holistic spatial parts, but its holistic temporal parts are not products. In other words, the individual must encompass the whole lifetime from creation to disposal.<br>A product can be a tangible object (e.g. a manufactured object), a process (e.g. service). It can be the outcome of a natural or an artificially driven process.<br>It must have and initial stage of its life that is also an outcome of a intentional process.</td>

  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Here we consider a temporal interval that is lower than the characteristic time of the physical process that provides the causality connection between the object parts.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">SubObject</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">An object which is an holistic temporal part of another object.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">If an inhabited house is considered as an house that is occupied by some people in its majority of time, then an interval of inhabited house in which occasionally nobody is in there is no more an inhabited house, but an unhinabited house, since this temporal part does not satisfy the criteria of the whole.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>

    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>

Number
^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_21f56795_ee72_4858_b571_11cfaa59c1a8">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_21f56795_ee72_4858_b571_11cfaa59c1a8</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A number individual provides the link between the ontology and the actual data, through the data property hasNumericalValue.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A number is actually a string (e.g. 1.4, 1e-8) of numerical digits and other symbols. However, in order not to increase complexity of the taxonomy and relations, here we take a number as an &quot;atomic&quot; object, without decomposit it in digits (i.e. we do not include digits in the EMMO as alphabet for numbers).</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">In math usually number and numeral are distinct concepts, the numeral being the symbol or a composition of symbols (e.g. 3.14, 010010, three) and the number is the idea behind it.<br>More than one numeral stands for the same number.<br>In the EMMO abstract entities do not exists, and numbers are simply defined by other numerals, so that a number is the class of all the numerals that are equivalent (e.g. 3 and 0011 are numerals that stands for the same number).<br>Or alternatively, an integer numeral may also stands for a set of a specific cardinality (e.g. 3 stands for a set of three apples). Rational and real numbers are simply a syntactic arrangment of integers (digits, in decimal system).<br>The fact that you can&#x27;t give a name to a number without using a numeral or, in case of positive integers, without referring to a real world objects set with specific cardinality, suggests that the abstract concept of number is not a concept that can be practically used.<br>For these reasons, the EMMO will consider numerals and numbers as the same concept.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Numeral</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Number</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A numerical data value.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_4ce76d7f_03f8_45b6_9003_90052a79bfaa">Numerical</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>

AmpereHour
^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>

    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#AmpereHour">https://w3id.org/emmo#AmpereHour</a></td>

  <tr>

  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Unitsymbol</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A⋅hr</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Qudtreference</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/A-HR">http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/A-HR</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Ucumcode</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A.h</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>

  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">AmpereHour</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">`Ampere hour` is a practical unit of electric charge equal to the charge flowing in one hour through a conductor passing one ampere. An ampere-hour or amp-hour (symbol Ah, AHr,  A · h, A h) is a unit of electric charge, with sub-units milliampere-hour (mAh) and milliampere second (mAs). One ampere-hour is equal to 3600 coulombs (ampere-seconds), the electric charge transferred by a steady current of one ampere for one hour. The ampere-hour is frequently used in measurements of electrochemical systems such as electroplating and electrical batteries. The commonly seen milliampere-hour (mAh or mA · h) is one-thousandth of an ampere-hour (3.6  coulombs).<br><br>-- QUDT</td>
  </tr>

The symbol ua is recommended by the International Bureau of Weights and Measures, and the international standard ISO 80000, while au is recommended by the International Astronomical Union, and is more common in Anglosphere countries. In general, the International System of Units only uses capital letters for the symbols of units which are named after individual scientists, while au or a.u. can also mean atomic unit or even arbitrary unit. However, the use of AU to refer to the astronomical unit is widespread. The astronomical constant whose value is one astronomical unit is referred to as unit distance and is given the symbol A.     <td class="element-table-value">Cubic Meter Per Hour (m3/h) is a unit in the category of Volume flow rate. It is also known as cubic meters per hour, cubic metre per hour, cubic metres per hour, cubic meter/hour, cubic metre/hour, cubic meter/hr, cubic metre/hr, flowrate. Cubic Meter Per Hour (m3/h) has a dimension of L3T-1 where L is length, and T is time. It can be converted to the corresponding standard SI unit m3/s by multiplying its value by a factor of 0.00027777777.<br><br>-- QUDT</td>
  </tr>

    <td class="element-table-value">An electron volt (eV) is the energy that an electron gains when it travels through a potential of one volt. You can imagine that the electron starts at the negative plate of a parallel plate capacitor and accelerates to the positive plate, which is at one volt higher potential. Numerically 1 eV approximates 1.6x10⁻¹⁹ joules, where 1 joule is 6.2x10¹⁸ eV. For example, it would take 6.2x10²⁰ eV/sec to light a 100 watt light bulb.<br><br>-- QUDT</td>

  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Definition</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The amount of energy gained (or lost) by the charge of a single electron moving across an electric potential difference of one volt.</td>

    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The neper is a logarithmic unit for ratios of measurements of physical field and power quantities, such as gain and loss of electronic signals. It has the unit symbol Np. The unit&#x27;s name is derived from the name of John Napier, the inventor of logarithms. As is the case for the decibel and bel, the neper is not a unit in the International System of Units (SI), but it is accepted for use alongside the SI. Like the decibel, the neper is a unit in a logarithmic scale. While the bel uses the decadic (base-10) logarithm to compute ratios, the neper uses the natural logarithm, based on Euler&#x27;s number<br><br>-- QUDT</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Wikipediareference</span></td>

  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Definition</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Unit of measurement for quantities of type level or level difference, which are defined as the natural logarithm of the ratio of power- or field-type quantities.<br><br>The value of a ratio in nepers is given by `ln(x1/x2)` where `x1` and `x2` are the values of interest (amplitudes), and ln is the natural logarithm. When the values are quadratic in the amplitude (e.g. power), they are first linearised by taking the square root before the logarithm is taken, or equivalently the result is halved.<br><br>Wikipedia</td>
  </tr>

    <td class="element-table-value">A square degree is a non-SI unit measure of solid angle. It is denoted in various ways, including deg, sq. deg. and °². Just as degrees are used to measure parts of a circle, square degrees are used to measure parts of a sphere. Analogous to one degree being equal to π /180 radians, a square degree is equal to (π /180) or about 1/3283 steradian. The number of square degrees in a whole sphere is or approximately 41 253 deg. This is the total area of the 88 constellations in the list of constellations by area. For example, observed from the surface of the Earth, the Moon has a diameter of approximately 0.5°, so it covers a solid angle of approximately 0.196 deg, which is 4.8 × 10 of the total sky sphere.<br><br>-- QUDT</td>

    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_47338839_6cca_4a8e_b565_3c4d5517e2c0">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_47338839_6cca_4a8e_b565_3c4d5517e2c0</a></td>

  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A chemical entity comprises the two different ways to represents matter: as single recognizable particle entity (molecular entity) and as a composition of particle entities (substance).<br><br>This distinction is not well assessed in actual chemical nomenclature, in which an element name refers to both the pure elemental substance or the atom.<br><br>In the EMMO we force the adoption of a more strict categorization based on mereotopology.<br><br>The class Material hosts the subclasses for which a substance can be identified without necessarily considering its nature of molecule/atom or substance (e.g. hydrocarbon is the class of both hydrocarbon molecules or gases).</td>
  </tr>

String
^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_50ea1ec5_f157_41b0_b46b_a9032f17ca10">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_50ea1ec5_f157_41b0_b46b_a9032f17ca10</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A string is made of concatenated symbols whose arrangement is one-dimensional. Each symbol can have only one previous and one next neighborhood (bidirectional list).</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A string is not requested to respect any syntactic rule: it&#x27;s simply directly made of symbols.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">String</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A physical made of more than one symbol sequentially arranged.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The word &quot;cat&quot; considered as a collection of &#x27;symbol&#x27;-s respecting the rules of english language.<br><br>In this example the &#x27;symbolic&#x27; entity &quot;cat&quot; is not related to the real cat, but it is only a word (like it would be to an italian person that ignores the meaning of this english word).<br><br>If an &#x27;interpreter&#x27; skilled in english language is involved in a &#x27;semiotic&#x27; process with this word, that &quot;cat&quot; became also a &#x27;sign&#x27; i.e. it became for the &#x27;interpreter&#x27; a representation for a real cat.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_89a0c87c_0804_4013_937a_6fe234d9499c">SymbolicConstruct</a></td>

Symbol
^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_a1083d0a_c1fb_471f_8e20_a98f881ad527">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_a1083d0a_c1fb_471f_8e20_a98f881ad527</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Subclasses of &#x27;Symbol&#x27; are alphabets, in formal languages terminology. A &#x27;Symbol&#x27; is atomic for that alphabet, i.e. it has no parts that are symbols for the same alphabet.<br>e.g. a math symbol is not made of other math symbols<br>A Symbol may be a String in another language.<br>e.g. &quot;Bq&quot; is the symbol for Becquerel units when dealing with metrology, or a string of &quot;B&quot; and &quot;q&quot; symbols when dealing with characters.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Symbols of a formal language need not be symbols of anything. For instance there are logical constants which do not refer to any idea, but rather serve as a form of punctuation in the language (e.g. parentheses).<br><br>Symbols of a formal language must be capable of being specified without any reference to any interpretation of them.<br>(Wikipedia)</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The class is the idea of the symbol, while the individual of that class stands for a specific mark (or token) of that idea.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">AlphabeticEntity</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Symbol</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The class of individuals that stand for an elementary mark of a specific symbolic code (alphabet).</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The class of letter &quot;A&quot; is the symbol as idea and the letter A that you see on the screen is the mark that can be represented by an individual belonging to &quot;A&quot;.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>

Symbolic
^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_057e7d57_aff0_49de_911a_8861d85cef40">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_057e7d57_aff0_49de_911a_8861d85cef40</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A symbolic entity is not necessarily graphical (e.g. it doesn&#x27;t necessarily have the physical shape of a letter), but its elements can be decoded and put in relation with an alphabet.<br>In other words, a sequence of bit &quot;1000010&quot; in a RAM (a non-graphical entity) is a valid symbol since it can be decoded through ASCII rules as the letter &quot;B&quot;. The same holds for an entity standing for the sound of a voice saying: &quot;Hello&quot;, since it can be decomposed in discrete parts, each of them being associated to a letter of an alphabet.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A symbolic object possesses a reductionistic oriented structure.<br>For example, text is made of words, spaces and punctuations. Words are made of characters (i.e. atomic symbols).</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The structure of an array can be expressed mereologically. An array consists of a set of equally sized tiles. The tiles of an n-dimensional array are (n-1)-dimensional,<br>the tiles of an (n-1)-dimensional array are (n-2)-dimensional and so forth...<br>The tiles of a vector (1-dimensional array) are scalar symbolic data (that is symbolic data that are not subclasses of array).<br><br>The `hasSpatialTile` relation, can be used to navigate between dimensions.<br><br>The `hasPart` relation can be used to refer to the scalar data</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Symbolic</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A discrete data whose elements can be decoded as tokens from one or more alphabets, without necessarily respecting syntactic rules.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">fe780<br>emmo<br>!5*a<br>cat<br>for(i=0;i&lt;N;++i)</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Equivalent To</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_89a0c87c_0804_4013_937a_6fe234d9499c">SymbolicConstruct</a> or <a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_a1083d0a_c1fb_471f_8e20_a98f881ad527">Symbol</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_be8592a7_68d1_4a06_ad23_82f2b56ef926">DiscreteData</a></td>
  </tr>

Classes

Holistic
^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_0277f24a_ea7f_4917_81b7_fb0406c8fc62">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_0277f24a_ea7f_4917_81b7_fb0406c8fc62</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Wholistic</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Holistic</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A perspective characterized by the belief that:<br>- a whole is more than merely the sum of its parts (wholism)<br>- the parts of a whole are interconnected in a way that can be explained only by reference to the whole (rolism).</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A molecule of a body can have role in the body evolution, without caring if its part of a specific organ and without specifying the time interval in which this role occurred.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A product is a role that can be fulfilled by many objects, but always requires a process to which the product participates and from which it is generated.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Definition</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The union of classes whole and part.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Conceptualisation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">An holistic perspective considers each part of the whole as equally important, without the need to position the parts within a hierarchy (in time or space). The interest is on the whole object and on its parts (how they contribute to the whole, i.e. their roles), without going further into specifying the spatial hierarchy or the temporal position of each part.<br><br>This class allows the picking of parts without necessarily going trough a rigid hierarchy of spatial compositions (e.g. body -&gt; organ -&gt; cell -&gt; molecule) or temporal composition. This is inline with the transitive nature of parthood, as it is usually defined in literature.<br><br>The holistic perspective is not excluding the reductionistic perspective, on the contrary it can be considered its complement.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Equivalent To</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_56cf1cea_bb26_4093_b587_dd64e230bf9b">QualifiedRole</a> or <a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_a374f1d4_55b1_4796_a8c6_88668f205cd2">QualifiedWhole</a></td>

holisticOverlaps
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_53e5b1e1_6026_4ddc_8a4a_3aaaa5fdbdb7">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_53e5b1e1_6026_4ddc_8a4a_3aaaa5fdbdb7</a></td>

  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">This relation is about two wholes that overlap, and whose intersection is an holistic part of both.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">holisticOverlaps</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A relation between two holistic wholes that properly overlap, sharing one of their holistic parts.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A man and the process of building a house.<br>The man is a whole that possesses an holistic temporal part which is an interval of six monts and represents a working period in his lifetime.<br>The process of building a house is a whole that possesses an holistic spatial part which is a builder.<br>The working period of the man and the builder participating the building process are the same individual, belonging both to a man lifetime and to a building holistic views.<br>In this sense, the man and the building process overcrosses. and the overlapping individual is represented differently in both holistic views.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>

    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>

BondedObject
^^^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_801395f8_948e_4637_ac3b_5fcd587d72ca">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_801395f8_948e_4637_ac3b_5fcd587d72ca</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">&quot;... in the &#x27;classical&#x27; picture ordinary matter is made of atoms, in which electrons are held in orbit around a nucleus of protons and neutrons by the electrical attraction of opposite charges. We can now give this model a more sophisticated formulation by attributing the binding force to the exchange of photons between the electrons and the protons in the nucleus. However, for the purposes of atomic physics this is overkill, for in this context quantization of the electromagnetic field produces only minute effects (notably the Lamb shift and the anomalous magnetic moment of the electron). To excellent approximation we can pretend that the forces are given by Coulomb&#x27;s law (together with various magnetic dipole couplings). The point is that in a bound state enormous numbers of photons are continually streaming back and forth, so that the &quot;lumpiness&quot; of the field is effectively smoothed out, and classical electrodynamics is a suitable approximation to the truth. But in most elementary particle processes, such as the photoelectric effect or Compton scattering, individual photons are involved, and quantization can no longer be ignored.&quot;<br>D. Griffiths, &quot;Introduction to elementary Particles&quot;, Wiley-VCH, 2004, pp.16-17</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">BondedObject</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Conceptualisation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A bonded object is a sequence of fundamental interactions that can be described approximatively by Schrodinger formulation. A bonded object is typically characterised by having quantum states (e.g.  electron states in an atom, energy levels of a molecule). Furthermore, a bonded object is made of elementary particles that travels from the beginning to the end of the entity (i.e. a bonded object doesn&#x27;t change its components).</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#Thing">Thing</a></td>
  </tr>
  </table>

Matter
^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_5b2222df_4da6_442f_8244_96e9e45887d1">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_5b2222df_4da6_442f_8244_96e9e45887d1</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A matter entity requires the presence of fermions without excluding the presence of real or virtual fundamental bosons parts that are responsible for the interactions between the (real) fundamental fermions.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Matter includes ordinary- and anti-matter. It is possible to have entities that are made of particle and anti-particles (e.g. mesons made of a quark and an anti-quark pair) so that it is possible to have entities that are somewhat heterogeneous with regards to this distinction.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">PhysicalSubstance</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Matter</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The class of physical objects that have some fermionic quantum parts.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Conceptualisation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The interpretation of the term &quot;matter&quot; is not univocal. Several concepts are labelled with this term, depending on the field of science. The concept mass is sometimes related to the term &quot;matter&quot;, even if the former refers to a physical quantity (precisely defined by modern physics) while the latter is a type that qualifies a physical entity.<br>It is possible to identify more than one concept that can be reasonably labelled with the term &quot;matter&quot;. For example, it is possible to label as matter only the entities that are made up of atoms. Or more generally, we can be more fine-grained and call &quot;matter&quot; the entities that are made up of protons, neutrons or electrons, so that we can call matter also a neutron radiation or a cathode ray.<br>A more fundamental approach, that we embrace for the EMMO, considers matter as entities that are made of fermions (i.e. quarks and leptons) requiring their presence, without excluding particles like the W and Z bosons that possess some mass, but are not fermions.<br>Antimatter is a subclass of matter.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_38b579de_4331_40e0_803d_09efa298e726">PhysicalObject</a></td>
  </tr>
  </table>

Molecule
^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_3397f270_dfc1_4500_8f6f_4d0d85ac5f71">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_3397f270_dfc1_4500_8f6f_4d0d85ac5f71</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">An entity is called essential if removing one direct part will lead to a change in entity class.<br>An entity is called redundand if removing one direct part will not lead to a change in entity class.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">This definition states that this object is a non-periodic set of atoms or a set with a finite periodicity.<br>Removing an atom from the state will result in another type of atom_based state.<br>e.g. you cannot remove H from H₂0 without changing the molecule type (essential). However, you can remove a C from a nanotube (redundant). C60 fullerene is a molecule, since it has a finite periodicity and is made of a well defined number of atoms (essential). A C nanotube is not a molecule, since it has an infinite periodicity (redundant).</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">ChemicalSubstance</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Molecule</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">An atom_based state defined by an exact number of e-bonded atomic species and an electron cloud made of the shared electrons.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">H₂0, C₆H₁₂O₆, CH₄</td>
  </tr>

    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>

PhysicalObject
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_38b579de_4331_40e0_803d_09efa298e726">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_38b579de_4331_40e0_803d_09efa298e726</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">PhysicalObject</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The class of individuals standing for causally convex interacting systems.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Conceptualisation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">It is natural to define entities made or more than one smaller parts as object according to some unity criteria. One of the most general one applicable to causal interacting systems is to ask that all the quantum parts of the system are part of elementaries whose paths start and end within the entitiy. We call this causal convexity. In other words, causal convexity excludes all quantums that leave the system (no more interacting), or that are not yet part of it (not yet interacting).<br>So, a photon leaving a body is not part of a convex system, while a real photon that is the carrier of clasical electromagnetic interaction between two molecular parts of the body, is part of the convex body.<br>A physical phenomenon is defined as a causally non-convex interacting system, complement of causally convex interacting system.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#Thing">Thing</a></td>
  </tr>

SIDimensionalUnit
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_9895a1b4_f0a5_4167_ac5e_97db40b8bfcc">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_9895a1b4_f0a5_4167_ac5e_97db40b8bfcc</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">In SI are the physical dimensions of the base quantities time (T), length (L), mass (M), electric current (I), thermodynamic temperature (Θ), amount of substance (N) and luminous intensity (J).<br><br>In general the dimension of any quantity Q is written in the form of a dimensional product,<br><br>    dim Q = T^α L^β M^γ I^δ Θ^ε N^ζ J^η<br><br>where the exponents α, β, γ, δ, ε, ζ and η, which are generally small integers, which can be positive, negative, or zero, are called the dimensional exponents.<br>-- SI brouchure<br><br>The SI dimensional units are equivalent to dimensional strings that uniquely defines their dimensionality by specifying the values of the coefficients α, β, γ, δ, ε, ζ and η. A dimensional string is a space-separated string of the physical dimension symbols followed by the value of the exponent (including it sign). They should always match the following regular expression:<br><br>^T([+-][1-9]|0) L([+-][1-9]|0) M([+-][1-9]|0) I([+-][1-9]|0) Θ([+-][1-9]|0) N([+-][1-9]|0) J([+-][1-9]|0)$<br><br>Examples of correspondance between dimensional units and their dimensional units are:<br><br>- AmountOfSubstanceUnit &lt;=&gt; &quot;T0 L0 M0 I0 Θ0 N+1 J0&quot;<br>- TimeUnit &lt;=&gt; &quot;T+1 L0 M0 I0 Θ0 N0 J0&quot;<br>- ElectricCurrentDensityUnit &lt;=&gt; &quot;T0 L-2 M0 I+1 Θ0 N0 J0&quot;</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">SIDimensionalUnit</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Dimensional unit with its physical dimensionality described accortind to the International System of Units (SI).</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The class of units with dimensionality &#x27;SIDimensional&#x27;.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>

Becquerel
^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#Becquerel">https://w3id.org/emmo#Becquerel</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iupacreference</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://doi.org/10.1351/goldbook.B00624">https://doi.org/10.1351/goldbook.B00624</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Qudtreference</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/BQ">http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/BQ</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Unececommoncode</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">BQL</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Ucumcode</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Bq</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The SI derived unit of activity, usually meaning radioactivity. &quot;Radioactivity&quot; is caused when atoms disintegrate, ejecting energetic particles. One becquerel is the radiation caused by one disintegration per second; this is equivalent to about 27.0270 picocuries (pCi). The unit is named for a French physicist, Antoine-Henri Becquerel (1852-1908), the discoverer of radioactivity. Note: both the becquerel and the hertz are basically defined as one event per second, yet they measure different things. The hertz is used to measure the rates of events that happen periodically in a fixed and definite cycle. The becquerel is used to measure the rates of events that happen sporadically and unpredictably, not in a definite cycle.<br><br>-- QUDT</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Becquerel</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">SI unit for radioactive activity.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Wikipediareference</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Becquerel?oldid=493710036">http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Becquerel?oldid=493710036</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Definition</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Radioactive decays per second.</td>

Electricity is actually a flow of charged particles, such as electrons, protons, or ions. The charge on one of these particles is a whole-number multiple of the charge e on a single electron, and one coulomb represents a charge of approximately 6.241 506 x 1018 e. The coulomb is named for a French physicist, Charles-Augustin de Coulomb (1736-1806), who was the first to measure accurately the forces exerted between electric charges.<br><br>-- QUDT</td>

   <div id="DegreeCelsius"></div>

DegreeCelsius
^^^^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#DegreeCelsius">https://w3id.org/emmo#DegreeCelsius</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iupacreference</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://doi.org/10.1351/goldbook.D01561">https://doi.org/10.1351/goldbook.D01561</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Qudtreference</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/DEG_C">http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/DEG_C</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Unececommoncode</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">CEL</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Ucumcode</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Cel</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Celsius, also known as centigrade, is a scale and unit of measurement for temperature. It can refer to a specific temperature on the Celsius scale as well as a unit to indicate a temperature interval, a difference between two temperatures or an uncertainty. This definition fixes the magnitude of both the degree Celsius and the kelvin as precisely 1 part in 273.16 (approximately 0.00366) of the difference between absolute zero and the triple point of water. Thus, it sets the magnitude of one degree Celsius and that of one kelvin as exactly the same. Additionally, it establishes the difference between the two scales&#x27; null points as being precisely 273.15 °C.<br><br>-- QUDT</td>
  </tr>

    <td class="element-table-value">Farad</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The SI unit of electric capacitance. Very early in the study of electricity scientists discovered that a pair of conductors separated by an insulator can store a much larger charge than an isolated conductor can store. The better the insulator, the larger the charge that the conductors can hold. This property of a circuit is called capacitance, and it is measured in farads. One farad is defined as the ability to store one coulomb of charge per volt of potential difference between the two conductors. This is a natural definition, but the unit it defines is very large. In practical circuits, capacitance is often measured in microfarads, nanofarads, or sometimes even in picofarads (10⁻¹² farad, or trillionths of a farad). The unit is named for the British physicist Michael Faraday (1791-1867), who was known for his work in electricity and electrochemistry.<br><br>-- QUDT</td>
  </tr>

  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Unececommoncode</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">81</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Ucumcode</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">H</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">H = Wb/A = V·s/A = Ω·s</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The SI unit of electric inductance. A changing magnetic field induces an electric current in a loop of wire (or in a coil of many loops) located in the field. Although the induced voltage depends only on the rate at which the magnetic flux changes, measured in webers per second, the amount of the current depends also on the physical properties of the coil. A coil with an inductance of one henry requires a flux of one weber for each ampere of induced current. If, on the other hand, it is the current which changes, then the induced field will generate a potential difference within the coil: if the inductance is one henry a current change of one ampere per second generates a potential difference of one volt. The henry is a large unit; inductances in practical circuits are measured in millihenrys (mH) or microhenrys (μH). The unit is named for the American physicist Joseph Henry (1797-1878), one of several scientists who discovered independently how magnetic fields can be used to generate alternating currents.<br><br>-- QUDT</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Henry</td>

    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">SI unit for electrical inductance.</td>

    <td class="element-table-value">The SI unit for measuring the flux of light being produced by a light source or received by a surface. The intensity of a light source is measured in candelas. One lumen represents the total flux of light emitted, equal to the intensity in candelas multiplied by the solid angle in steradians into which the light is emitted. A full sphere has a solid angle of 4·π steradians. A light source that uniformly radiates one candela in all directions has a total luminous flux of 1 cd·4π sr = 4π cd·sr ≈ 12.57 lumens. &quot;Lumen&quot; is a Latin word for light.<br><br>-- QUDT</td>

    <td class="element-table-value">The SI unit for measuring the illumination (illuminance) of a surface. One lux is defined as an illumination of one lumen per square meter or 0.0001 phot. In considering the various light units, it&#x27;s useful to think about light originating at a point and shining upon a surface. The intensity of the light source is measured in candelas; the total light flux in transit is measured in lumens (1 lumen = 1 candelau·steradian); and the amount of light received per unit of surface area is measured in lux (1 lux = 1 lumen/square meter). One lux is equal to approximately 0.09290 foot candle.<br><br>-- QUDT</td>

    <td class="element-table-value">The mole, symbol mol, is the SI unit of amount of substance. One mole contains exactly 6.022 140 76 × 1023 elementary entities. This number is the fixed numerical value of the Avogadro constant, NA, when expressed in the unit mol−1 and is called the Avogadro number. The amount of substance, symbol n, of a system is a measure of the number of specified elementary entities. An elementary entity may be an atom, a molecule, an ion, an electron, any other particle or specified group of particles.</td>

  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>

  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Qudtreference</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/S">http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/S</a></td>

  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Unececommoncode</span></td>

    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Ucumcode</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">S</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Siemens  is the SI unit of electric conductance, susceptance, and admittance. The most important property of a conductor is the amount of current it will carry when a voltage is applied. Current flow is opposed by resistance in all circuits, and by also by reactance and impedance in alternating current circuits. Conductance, susceptance, and admittance are the inverses of resistance, reactance, and impedance, respectively. To measure these properties, the siemens is the reciprocal of the ohm. In other words, the conductance, susceptance, or admittance, in siemens, is simply 1 divided by the resistance, reactance or impedance, respectively, in ohms. The unit is named for the German electrical engineer Werner von Siemens (1816-1892).<br><br>-- QUDT</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>

    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The SI unit of flux density (or field intensity) for magnetic fields (also called the magnetic induction). The intensity of a magnetic field can be measured by placing a current-carrying conductor in the field. The magnetic field exerts a force on the conductor, a force which depends on the amount of the current and on the length of the conductor. One tesla is defined as the field intensity generating one newton of force per ampere of current per meter of conductor. Equivalently, one tesla represents a magnetic flux density of one weber per square meter of area. A field of one tesla is quite strong: the strongest fields available in laboratories are about 20 teslas, and the Earth&#x27;s magnetic flux density, at its surface, is about 50 microteslas. The tesla, defined in 1958, honors the Serbian-American electrical engineer Nikola Tesla (1856-1943), whose work in electromagnetic induction led to the first practical generators and motors using alternating current.<br><br>-- QUDT</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">T = V·s·m⁻² = N/(A·m) = Wb/m</td>

  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The SI unit of power. Power is the rate at which work is done, or (equivalently) the rate at which energy is expended. One watt is equal to a power rate of one joule of work per second of time. This unit is used both in mechanics and in electricity, so it links the mechanical and electrical units to one another. In mechanical terms, one watt equals about 0.001 341 02 horsepower (hp) or 0.737 562 foot-pound per second (lbf/s). In electrical terms, one watt is the power produced by a current of one ampere flowing through an electric potential of one volt. The name of the unit honors James Watt (1736-1819), the British engineer whose improvements to the steam engine are often credited with igniting the Industrial Revolution.<br><br>-- QUDT</td>

  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iupacreference</span></td>

    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Ucumcode</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Wb</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The SI unit of magnetic flux. &quot;Flux&quot; is the rate (per unit of time) at which something crosses a surface perpendicular to the flow. The weber is a large unit, equal to 10⁸ maxwells, and practical fluxes are usually fractions of one weber. The weber is the magnetic flux which, linking a circuit of one turn, would produce in it an electromotive force of 1 volt if it were reduced to zero at a uniform rate in 1 second. In SI base units, the dimensions of the weber are (kg·m²)/(s²·A). The weber is commonly expressed in terms of other derived units as the Tesla-square meter (T·m²), volt-seconds (V·s), or joules per ampere (J/A).</td>
  </tr>

ContinuumSubstance
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_8b0923ab_b500_477b_9ce9_8b3a3e4dc4f2">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_8b0923ab_b500_477b_9ce9_8b3a3e4dc4f2</a></td>

  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A continuum is made of a sufficient number of parts that it continues to exists as continuum individual even after the loss of one of them i.e. a continuum is a redundant.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A continuum is not necessarily small (i.e. composed by the minimum amount of sates to fulfill the definition).<br><br>A single continuum individual can be the whole fluid in a pipe.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A continuum is the bearer of properties that are generated by the interactions of parts such as viscosity and thermal or electrical conductivity.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">ContinuumSubstance</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A state that is a collection of sufficiently large number of other parts such that:<br>- it is the bearer of qualities that can exists only by the fact that it is a sum of parts<br>- the smallest partition dV of the state volume in which we are interested in, contains enough parts to be statistically consistent: n [#/m3] x dV [m3] &gt;&gt; 1</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>

PhaseOfMatter
^^^^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_668fbd5b_6f1b_405c_9c6b_d6067bd0595a">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_668fbd5b_6f1b_405c_9c6b_d6067bd0595a</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">In the physical sciences, a phase is a region of space (a thermodynamic system), throughout which all physical properties of a material are essentially uniform. Examples of physical properties include density, index of refraction, magnetization and chemical composition. A simple description is that a phase is a region of material that is chemically uniform, physically distinct, and (often) mechanically separable. In a system consisting of ice and water in a glass jar, the ice cubes are one phase, the water is a second phase, and the humid air is a third phase over the ice and water. The glass of the jar is another separate phase.<br><br>The term phase is sometimes used as a synonym for state of matter, but there can be several immiscible phases of the same state of matter. Also, the term phase is sometimes used to refer to a set of equilibrium states demarcated in terms of state variables such as pressure and temperature by a phase boundary on a phase diagram. Because phase boundaries relate to changes in the organization of matter, such as a change from liquid to solid or a more subtle change from one crystal structure to another, this latter usage is similar to the use of &quot;phase&quot; as a synonym for state of matter. However, the state of matter and phase diagram usages are not commensurate with the formal definition given above and the intended meaning must be determined in part from the context in which the term is used.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Phase</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">PhaseOfMatter</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A matter object throughout which all physical properties of a material are essentially uniform.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_8b0923ab_b500_477b_9ce9_8b3a3e4dc4f2">ContinuumSubstance</a></td>
  </tr>

  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The fact that there may be a finite granularity in the variations of the material basis (e.g. the smallest peak in a vynil that can be recognized by the piezo-electric transducer) does not prevent a data to be analog. It means only that the focus on such data encoding is on a scale that makes such variations negligible, making them practically a continuum.</td>

Contrast
^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>

  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A data is a causal object whose variations (non-uniformity) can be recognised and eventually interpreted.<br>A data can be of different physical types (e.g., matter, wave, atomic excited states).<br>How the variations are recognised and eventually decoded depends on the interpreting rules that characterise that type of data.<br>Variations are pure physical variations and do not necessarily possess semantic meaning.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The covering axiom that defines the data class discriminates within all the possible causal objects between encoded or non encoded.</td>
