Data
^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_3e7add3d_e6ed_489a_a796_8e31fef9b490">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_3e7add3d_e6ed_489a_a796_8e31fef9b490</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">EncodedData is the class where inventions that don&#x27;t actually exist whould be placed.<br>For example, the blueprint of a bridge is an encoded data. When the bridge will be built, than the blueprint will also be a semiotical entity.<br>Another example is Superman, that exists only as a set of magazines, drawings, novels, movies, but not in the real world.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Variations in data are generated by an agent (not necessarily human) and are intended to be decoded by the same or another agent using the same encoding rules.<br>Data are always generated by an agent but not necessarily possess a semantic meaninig, either because it&#x27;s lost or unknown or because simply they possess none (e.g. a random generation of symbols). A data object may be used as the physical basis for a sign, under Semiotics perspective.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">We call &quot;decoding&quot; the act of recognise the variation according to a particular rule and generate another equivalent schema (e.g. in the agent&#x27;s cognitive apparatus, as another form of data).<br>We call &quot;interpreting&quot; the act of providing semantic meaning to data, which is covered by the semiotic perspective.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">EncodedContrast</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">EncodedData</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Data</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A causal object whose properties variation are encoded by an agent and that can be decoded by another agent according to a specific rule.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A Radio Morse Code transmission can be addressed by combination of perspectives.<br>Physicalistic: the electromagnetic pulses can be defined as individual A (of type Field) and the strip of paper coming out a printer receiver can be defined as individual B (of type Matter).<br>Data: both A and B are also DiscreteData class individuals. In particular they may belong to a MorseData class, subclass of DiscreteData.<br>Perceptual: B is an individual belonging to the graphical entities expressing symbols. In particular is a formula under the MorseLanguage class, made of a combination of . and - symbols.<br>Semiotics: A and B can be signs if they refers to something else (e.g. a report about a fact, names).</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A signal through a cable. A sound wave. Words on a page. The pattern of excited states within a computer RAM.</td>

Arrangement
^^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_36c79456_e29c_400d_8bd3_0eedddb82652">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_36c79456_e29c_400d_8bd3_0eedddb82652</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The definition of an arrangement implies that its spatial direct parts are not gained or lost during its temporal extension (they exist from the left to the right side of the time interval), so that the cardinality of spatial direct parts in an arrangement is constant.<br>This does not mean that there cannot be a change in the internal structure of the arrangement direct parts. It means only that this change must not affect the existence of the direct part itself.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The use of spatial direct parthood in state definition means that an arrangement cannot overlap in space another arrangement that is direct part of the same whole.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">MereologicalState</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Arrangement</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A causal object which is tessellated with only spatial direct parts.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">e.g. the existent in my glass is declared at t = t_start as made of two direct parts: the ice and the water. It will continue to exists as state as long as the ice is completely melt at t = t_end. The new state will be completely made of water. Between t_start and t_end there is an exchange of molecules between the ice and the water, but this does not affect the existence of the two states.<br><br>If we partition the existent in my glass as ice surrounded by several molecules (we do not use the object water as direct part) then the appearance of a molecule coming from the ice will cause a state to end and another state to begin.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Conceptualisation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/emmo-repo/EMMO/1.0.0-rc1/doc/figs/Arrangement.png">https://raw.githubusercontent.com/emmo-repo/EMMO/1.0.0-rc1/doc/figs/Arrangement.png</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_8944581c_64da_46a9_be29_7074f7cc8098">SpatialTiling</a></td>
  </tr>
  </table>

Existent
^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_52211e5e_d767_4812_845e_eb6b402c476a">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_52211e5e_d767_4812_845e_eb6b402c476a</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">&#x27;Existent&#x27; is the EMMO class to be used for representing real world physical objects under a reductionistic perspective (i.e. objects come from the composition of sub-part objects, both in time and space).<br><br>&#x27;Existent&#x27; class collects all individuals that stand for physical objects that can be structured in well defined temporal sub-parts called states, through the temporal direct parthood relation.<br><br>This class provides a first granularity hierarchy in time, and a way to axiomatize tessellation principles for a specific whole with a non-transitivity relation (direct parthood) that helps to retain the granularity levels.<br><br>e.g. a car, a supersaturated gas with nucleating nanoparticles, an atom that becomes ionized and then recombines with an electron.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">An &#x27;Existent&#x27; individual stands for a real world object for which the ontologist wants to provide univocal tessellation in time.<br><br>By definition, the tiles are represented by &#x27;State&#x27;-s individual.<br><br>Tiles are related to the &#x27;Existent&#x27; through temporal direct parthood, enforcing non-transitivity and inverse-functionality.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Being hasTemporalDirectPart a proper parthood relation, there cannot be &#x27;Existent&#x27; made of a single &#x27;State&#x27;.<br><br>Moreover, due to inverse functionality, a &#x27;State&#x27; can be part of only one &#x27;Existent&#x27;, preventing overlapping between &#x27;Existent&#x27;-s.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Existent</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A &#x27;Physical&#x27; which is a tessellation of &#x27;State&#x27; temporal direct parts.</td>

A tiling is identified as a set of items {x1, x2, ... xn} called tiles that:<br>    - are proper parts of y<br>    - covers the entire whole (y = x1 +x2 + ... + xn)<br>    - do not overlap<br>    - are part of one, and one only, whole (inverse functional)</td>

  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">This relation is a simple collector of all relations inverse functional direct parthoods that can be defined in specialised theories using reductionism.</td>

    <td class="element-table-value">hasDirectPart</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The relation grouping all direct parthood relations used in the reductionistic perspective.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Conceptualisation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Direct parthood is the non transitive version of parthood enabling the establishment of hierarchy of granularities, starting with an entity and providing several tesselation levels according to specific criteria.<br>The criteria are implemented in specialised versions of the direct parthood relation (e.g., metrological direct part, XML format direct part).<br>The direct parts (tiles) and the tessellated entity (tessellation) are causally self connected (i.e., items), coherently with the concept behind the definition of the reductionistic perspective.</td>

In terms of notes, bottom C would be 0.25 volts, the next C up would be 0.5 volts, then 1V, 2V, 4V, 8V for the following octaves. This system was used mainly by Yamaha and Korg.<br><br>-- QUDT</td>

Division by the number of moles facilitates comparison between processes involving different quantities of material and between similar processes involving different types of materials.     <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The magnetic moment of a magnet is a quantity that determines the force that the magnet can exert on electric currents and the torque that a magnetic field will exert on it. A loop of electric current, a bar magnet, an electron, a molecule, and a planet all have magnetic moments. The unit for magnetic moment is not a base unit in the International System of Units (SI) and it can be represented in more than one way. For example, in the current loop definition, the area is measured in square meters and I is measured in amperes, so the magnetic moment is measured in ampere-square meters (A m2). In the equation for torque on a moment, the torque is measured in joules and the magnetic field in tesla, so the moment is measured in Joules per Tesla (J u00b7T-1). These two representations are equivalent: 1 A u00b7m2 = 1 J u00b7T-1.<br><br>-- QUDT</td>

    <td class="element-table-value">Thermal resistance is a heat property and a measure of a temperature difference by which an object or material resists a heat flow (heat per time unit or thermal resistance). It is the reciprocal of thermal conductance. The SI units of thermal resistance are kelvins per watt or the equivalent degrees Celsius per watt (the two are the same since as intervals).<br><br>-- QUDT</td>

It may be better understood when phrased as &quot;metres per second times metres&quot;, i.e. the momentum of an object with respect to a position.<br><br>-- QUDT</td>

FundamentalPhysicalSystem
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_43a4e80d_6ae9_45ed_8cfb_fd0a5339bf87">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_43a4e80d_6ae9_45ed_8cfb_fd0a5339bf87</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A fundamental system is expressed as a complete bipartite directed graph K(m,n) of quantums, m being the number of originating quantums, and n being the receiving quantums.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">FundamentalPhysicalSystem</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A causal system that is the representation of a Feynman diagram, where quantum represents the real particles entering and exiting the system.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Conceptualisation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A fundamental physical process is made of one or more standard particles as input, and one or more standard particles as output, where each input is direct cause of each output.<br>Each fundamental physical phenomena refers to a Feynman diagram, hence is made at least of three standard model particles.<br>This requirement implies that a physical phenomena is either a decay, annihilation, interaction, collapse or creation phenomena (fundamental) or a composition of them (non-fundamental).</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_e7aac247_31d6_4b2e_9fd2_e842b1b7ccac">CausalSystem</a></td>

  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Conceptualisation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A collection is the concept that complements the item concept, being an entity that possesses at least one part non directly causally connected with the rest.<br>A collection can be partitioned in maximally connected items called members. The members are self-connected entities and there is no direct causality relation between them.<br>The combination of collection and item concepts is the EMMO mereocausality alternative to set theory. However, two items can be members only if they are non direct causally connected, giving some constraints to a collection definition. For example, two entities which are directly connected cannot be two distinct members, while their interiors (i.e. the entities obtained by removing the layer of parts that provides the causal contact between them) can be.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>

EMMO
^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_802d3e92_8770_4f98_a289_ccaaab7fdddf">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_802d3e92_8770_4f98_a289_ccaaab7fdddf</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">EMMO entities dimensionality is related to their mereocausal structures. From the no-dimensional quantum entity, we introduce time dimension with the elementary concept, and the spacetime with the causal system concept.<br>The EMMO conceptualisation does not allow the existence of space without a temporal dimension, the latter coming from a causal relation between entities.<br>For this reason, the EMMO entities that are not quantum or elementaries, may be considered to be always spatiotemporal. The EMMO poses no constraints to the number of spatial dimensions for a causal system (except being higher than one).</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">EMMO</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The class of all the OWL individuals representing world entities according to EMMO conceptualisation.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Definition</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The disjoint union of the fundamental mereocausal classes of Quantum, CausalPath, CausalSystem and Collection.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Conceptualisation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The EMMO conceptualises the world using the primitive concepts of causality and parthood. Parthood is about the composition of world entities starting from other more fundamental entities. Causality is about the interactions between world entities.<br>The quantum is the smallest indivisible part of any world entity. Quantum individuals are the fundamental causal constituents of the universe, since it is implied that causality originates from quantum-to-quantum interactions. Quantums are no-dimensional, and their aggregation makes spacetime emerge from their causal structure. Causality between macro entities (i.e. entities made of more than one quantum) is explained as the sum of the causality relations between their quantum constituents. Fundamental interactions (quantum fields) are represented as symmetric causality between macro entities, while classical interactions are mediated by chain of quantums (i.e. elementary particles).<br>The fundamental distinction between world entities is direct causality self-connectedness: a world entity can be self-connected xor not self-connected depending on the causality network of its fundamental components.<br>Void regions do not exist in the EMMO, or in other words there is no spacetime without entities, since space and time are measured quantities following a causality relation between entities (spacetime emerges as relational property not as a self-standing entity).<br>Entities are not placed in space or time: space and time are always relative between entities and are measured. In other words, space and time relations originates from causality interactions.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#Thing">Thing</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_17e27c22_37e1_468c_9dd7_95e137f73e7f">hasPart</a> some <a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_3f9ae00e_810c_4518_aec2_7200e424cf68">Quantum</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Inverse(<a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_17e27c22_37e1_468c_9dd7_95e137f73e7f">hasPart</a>) value <a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_08cb807c_e626_447b_863f_e2835540e918">universe</a></td>
  </tr>
  </table>

Item
^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_eb3a768e_d53e_4be9_a23b_0714833c36de">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_eb3a768e_d53e_4be9_a23b_0714833c36de</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The concept of self-connectivity is applied using a 4D approach. Given that, the entity made of an electron and a proton that travel, interact, and then depart from each other is an item, since we don&#x27;t focus only on the beginning or the end stage but to the overall 4D entity, being the interaction the connectivity bridge between the two particles.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">CausalObject</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Item</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The class of individuals standing for quantum or causally self-connected world entities.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A person life, an interval of a person life. The lifetime of two components, from the production in separate manufacturing lines, their being connected components in a device, including their eparation and decommissioning.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Definition</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The disjoint union of Particle and CausalStructure classes.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Conceptualisation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A world entity is direct causally self-connected if any two parts that make up the whole are direct causally connected to each other. In the EMMO, topological connectivity is based on causality.<br>All physical objects, i.e. entities whose behaviour is explained by physics laws, are represented only by items. In other words, a physical object part is embedded in a direct causal graph that provides always a path between two of its parts.<br>Members of a collection lack such direct causality connection, i.e. they do not constitute a physical object.<br>Following graph theory concepts, the quantums of an item are all connected together within a network of causal relations, forming a connected causal graph. A collection is then a set of disconnected graphs.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Equivalent To</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_52b8a39b_e5ff_46d3_b972_65bc43077a07">CausalParticle</a> or <a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_c5ddfdba_c074_4aa4_ad6b_1ac4942d300d">CausalStructure</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>

Quantum
^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_3f9ae00e_810c_4518_aec2_7200e424cf68">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_3f9ae00e_810c_4518_aec2_7200e424cf68</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A quantum is the EMMO mereological atomistic and causal reductionistic entity.  To avoid confusion with the concept of atom coming from physics and to underline the causal reductionistic approach, we will use the expression quantum mereology, instead of atomistic mereology.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">RealParticle</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Quantum</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The class of the mereological and causal fundamental entities.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">From a physics perspective a quantum can be related to smallest identifiable entities, according to the limits imposed by the uncertainty principle in space and time measurements.<br>However, the quantum mereotopology approach is not restricted only to physics. For example, in a manpower management ontology, a quantum can stand for an hour (time) of a worker (space) activity.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Definition</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The class of entities without proper parts.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Conceptualisation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A quantum is the most fundamental item (both mereologically and causally) and is considered causally self-connected by definition.<br>The quantum concept recalls the fact that there is lower epistemological limit to our knowledge of the universe, related to the uncertainity principle.<br>Space and time emerge following the network of causal connections between quantum objects. So quantum objects are adimensional objects, that precede space and time dimensions: they are simple beings (in greek οντα).<br>Using physics concepts, we can think the quantum as an elementary particle (e.g. an electron) in a specific state between two causal interactions.<br>A quantum stands for an incoming or outcoming real particle in a Feynman diagram.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#Thing">Thing</a></td>
  </tr>
  </table>

contacts
^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_8785be5a_2493_4b12_8f39_31907ab11748">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_8785be5a_2493_4b12_8f39_31907ab11748</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Spatial contact is symmetric and irreflexive.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The contact relation is not an ordering relation since is symmetric.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">hasSpatialnteractionWith</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">contacts</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">An interaction that is the sum of direct causality relations between two entities that are interpretable as fundamental physical interactions.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">An elementary electron is in contact with another elementary electron in a scattering process.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The laptop is in contact with the desk, since there is a double-directional causality.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Conceptualisation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A spatial contact between two entities occurs when the two entities are in an interaction relation whose causal structure is a representation of the fundamental interactions between elementary particles (Feynman diagrams).<br>It means that if two entities are in contact, then there is at least a couple of elementary particles, one part of the first and one part of the second, interacting according to one of the fundamental interactions through virtual particles. This kind of connection is space-like (i.e. interconnecting force carrier particle is offshelf).<br>Contacts between two entities exclude the possibility of other causal relations that are not included in a fundamental space-like interaction.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#ObjectProperty">ObjectProperty</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#ObjectProperty">ObjectProperty</a></td>

hasNext
^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_499e24a5_5072_4c83_8625_fe3f96ae4a8d">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_499e24a5_5072_4c83_8625_fe3f96ae4a8d</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Each pair of entities in direct causality relation is either in hasNext or hasTwoWayCauseWith relation. The two are mutually exclusive.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">This relation is asymmetric and irreflexive.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">isBefore</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">hasNext</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A time contact occurs when x isDirectCause y and not(y isCauseOf x).</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">My life between 18-24 years has next my life between 24-32 years.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The raw sample has next the treated sampled, which has next the examined sample. In this sense the whole sample is made of three states, connected by the has next relation, following its evolution in time.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Conceptualisation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A temporal relation between two entities occurs when the two entities are in a one directional causality relation. The idea is that a temporal relation always implies a one-directional causality between two entities, leading to a asymmetric relation.<br>This means that the causing entity can be in direct and optionally indirect causality relation with the effect entity. On the contrary, the effect entity cannot be in any causal relation (direct or indirect) with the causing entity.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#ObjectProperty">ObjectProperty</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#ObjectProperty">ObjectProperty</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#ObjectProperty">ObjectProperty</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_555d0261_da5e_4301_b7f9_46f604a32e91">isDirectCauseOf</a></td>

   <div id="EMMO_d67ee67e_4fac_4676_82c9_aec361dba698"></div>

isCauseOf
^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_d67ee67e_4fac_4676_82c9_aec361dba698">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_d67ee67e_4fac_4676_82c9_aec361dba698</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Each pair of causally connected entities is either in isDirectCauseOf or isIndirectCauseOf relation. The two are mutually exclusive.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">It applies to both quantums and macro-entities (entities made of more than one quantum). It is admissible for two entities to be one the cause of the other, excepts when they are both quantums.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The OWL 2 DL version of the EMMO introduces this object property as primitive causal relation. It refers to the macro causality relation mC(x,y), defined in the EMMO FOL version. While the EMMO FOL introduces the quantum causality relation C(x,y) as primitive, the OWL 2 DL version substantially simplifies the theory, neglecting these lower level relations that are well above DL expressivity.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">isCauseOf</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The relation between an individuals x and y, that holds if and only if:<br>a) y having a part that is causing an effect on a part of x<br>b) y and x are non-overlapping</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">John yesterday is the cause of John today, is an example of temporal-like causality. The desk supporting my laptop is a space-like causality.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Conceptualisation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">We say that an entity causes another if there is a quantum part of the first that is in causal relation with a quantum parts of the second.<br>An entity cannot cause itself (causal loops are forbidden) or a part of itself. For this reasons causality between entities excludes reflexivity and prevents them to overlap.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#ObjectProperty">ObjectProperty</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#ObjectProperty">ObjectProperty</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_ad0e72fc_dcaa_490d_8371_b4d814dcda2c">causal</a></td>
  </tr>
  </table>

isDirectCauseOf
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_555d0261_da5e_4301_b7f9_46f604a32e91">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_555d0261_da5e_4301_b7f9_46f604a32e91</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Direct cause is irreflexive.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Direct cause provides the edges for the transitive restriction of the direct acyclic causal graph whose nodes are the quantum entities.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">isDirectCauseOf</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A causal relation between the causing and the effected entities occurring without intermediaries.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Conceptualisation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Direct causality is a concept that capture the idea of contact between two entities, given the fact that there are no causal intermediaries between them. It requires that at least a quantum of the causing entity is direct cause of a quantum of the caused entity.<br>It does not exclude the possibility of indirect causal routes between proper parts of the two entities.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>

Module: Persistence
===================



.. _persistence-classes:

Classes
-------

.. raw:: html

   <div id="EMMO_90ae56e4_d197_49b6_be1a_0049e4756606"></div>

Object
^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_90ae56e4_d197_49b6_be1a_0049e4756606">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_90ae56e4_d197_49b6_be1a_0049e4756606</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Indefinitely temporally slicing of an entity leads to temporal parts whose temporal extension is so small that the connectivity relations that define the entity as an item will no longer hold. More generally. a temporal part is no more of type ϕ when the temporal interval is lower than the interval that characterizes the causality interactions between the object parts.<br>In other terms, if the time span of a temporal part is lower than the inverse of the frequency of interactions between the constituents, then the constituents in such temporal part are not connected. The object is no more an object, neither an item, but simply a collection of fundamental quantum parts.<br>For this reason, the definition of object is done by considering only item temporal parts, meaning that slicing in time has the lower limit of a self-connected (i.e. item) entity.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Continuant</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Endurant</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Object</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The superclass for causal structure classes whose individuals have all temporal item parts of the same type of the whole.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Practically speaking, the Object class can be populated by primitive subclasses (e.g. Car) for each of which holds the axiom that all the item parts are of the same type of the whole (e.g. Car SubClassOf hasTemporalItemPart only Car).<br>The intended usage is not for an individual to belong directly to Object, but to belong to a specific subclass of Object that identifies entities with a type-persistent structure.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Conceptualisation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">An item can be classified as an object according to a type ϕ (a ϕ-object) if it&#x27;s a ϕ all its temporal item parts are also of type ϕ. This conceptualisation tries to catch the persistency of type in the temporal parts of an entity.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>

   <div id="EMMO_e04884d9_eda6_487e_93d5_7722d7eda96b"></div>

Persistence
^^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_e04884d9_eda6_487e_93d5_7722d7eda96b">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_e04884d9_eda6_487e_93d5_7722d7eda96b</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The persistence perspective classifies entities according to the persistence of temporal parts of specifc type, introducing the distiction between objects (when a type is conserved through all its time parts) or processes (where a type is not conserved through all its time parts).<br>This perspective provides classes aimed to represent concepts similar to the ones of endurant and perdurant (a.k.a. continuant and occurrent). However, in the EMMO case, an entity is defined as an object or a process according to a specific type, and not per-se. For this reason an entity in the EMMO can be classified both object or a process depending on the reference type, due to the underlying 4D framework (e.g. an individual may belong both to the class of runners and the class of running process), and the distinction is purely representational.<br>This categorisation has been introduced due to the large use of object/process commonsensical concepts, and the fact that our language distinguish between nouns and verbs to address things, forcing the separation between things that happens and things that persist.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Persistence</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The union of the object or process classes.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Equivalent To</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_43e9a05d_98af_41b4_92f6_00f79a09bfce">Process</a> or <a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_90ae56e4_d197_49b6_be1a_0049e4756606">Object</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_49267eba_5548_4163_8f36_518d65b583f9">Perspective</a></td>
  </tr>
  </table>

Process
^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_43e9a05d_98af_41b4_92f6_00f79a09bfce">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_43e9a05d_98af_41b4_92f6_00f79a09bfce</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A process can be defined only according to an entity type. The minimum process is an entity made of two entities of different types that are temporally related.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Following the common definition of process, the reader may think that every entity in the EMMO should be a process, since every 4D entity0 always has a time dimension. However, in the EMMO we restrict the concept of process to items whose temporal parts show a change in type (i.e. every 4D object unfolds in time, but not every 4D time unfolding may be of interest for the ontologist and categorized as a process).<br>The definition of every specific process subclass requires a reference type, that is expressed by some but not all temporal parts.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Occurrent</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Perdurant</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Process</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The superclass for causal structure classes whose individuals have some temporal item parts that are not of the same type of the whole.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Practically speaking, the Process class can be populated by primitive subclasses (e.g. Cooking) for each of which holds the axiom that not all the item temporal parts are of the same type of the whole (e.g. breaking an egg, which is not necessarily a cooking process) and there are at least two temporal item parts of different types (e.g. breaking and egg and turning on the stove).<br>The intended usage is not for an individual to belong directly to Process, but to belong to a specific subclass of Process that identifies entities with a specific non-type-persistent structure.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>

    <td class="element-table-value">A conventional referring to an object according to a specific code that reflects the results of a specific interaction mechanism and is shared between other interpreters.<br>A coded is always a partial representation of an object since it reflects the object capability to be part of a specific determination.<br>A coded is a sort of name or label that we put upon objects that interact with an determiner in the same specific way.<br><br>For example, &quot;hot&quot; objects are objects that interact with an observer through a perception mechanism aimed to perceive an heat source. The code is made of terms such as &quot;hot&quot;, &quot;warm&quot;, &quot;cold&quot;, that commonly refer to the perception of heat.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Let&#x27;s define the class Colour as the subclass of the coded signs that involve photon emission and electromagnetic radiation sensible observers.<br>An individual C of this class Colour can be defined be declaring the process individual (e.g. daylight illumination) and the observer (e.g. my eyes)<br>Stating that an entity E hasCoded C, we mean that it can be observed by such setup of process + observer (i.e. observed by my eyes under daylight).<br>This definition can be specialised for human eye perception, so that the observer can be a generic human, or to camera perception so that the observer can be a device.<br>This can be used in material characterization, to define exactly the type of measurement done, including the instrument type.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Coded</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A conventional that stands for an object according to a code of interpretation to which the interpreter refers.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A biography that makes use of a code that is provided by the meaning of the element of the language used by the author.</td>

SemioticEntity
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_b803f122_4acb_4064_9d71_c1e5fd091fc9">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_b803f122_4acb_4064_9d71_c1e5fd091fc9</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Semiotic subclasse are defined using Peirce&#x27;s semiotic theory.<br><br>&quot;Namely, a sign is something, A, which brings something, B, its interpretant sign determined or created by it, into the same sort of correspondence with something, C, its object, as that in which itself stands to C.&quot; (Peirce 1902, NEM 4, 20–21).<br><br>The triadic elements:<br>- &#x27;sign&#x27;: the sign A (e.g. a name)<br>- &#x27;interpretant&#x27;: the sign B as the effects of the sign A on the interpreter (e.g. the mental concept of what a name means)<br>- &#x27;object&#x27;: the object C (e.g. the entity to which the sign A and B refer to)<br><br>This class includes also the &#x27;interpeter&#x27; i.e. the entity that connects the &#x27;sign&#x27; to the &#x27;object&#x27;</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">SemioticEntity</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The class of individuals that stands for semiotic objects, i.e. objects that take part on a semiotic process.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Equivalent To</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_0527413c_b286_4e9c_b2d0_03fb2a038dee">Interpreter</a> or <a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_6f5af708_f825_4feb_a0d1_a8d813d3022b">SemioticObject</a> or <a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_b21a56ed_f969_4612_a6ec_cb7766f7f31d">Sign</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#Thing">Thing</a></td>
  </tr>

SemioticObject
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_6f5af708_f825_4feb_a0d1_a8d813d3022b">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_6f5af708_f825_4feb_a0d1_a8d813d3022b</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Here is assumed that the concept of &#x27;object&#x27; is always relative to a &#x27;semiotic&#x27; process. An &#x27;object&#x27; does not exists per se, but it&#x27;s always part of an interpretation.<br><br>The EMMO relies on strong reductionism, i.e. everything real is a formless collection of elementary particles: we give a meaning to real world entities only by giving them boundaries and defining them using &#x27;sign&#x27;-s.<br><br>In this way the &#x27;sign&#x27;-ed entity becomes an &#x27;object&#x27;, and the &#x27;object&#x27; is the basic entity needed in order to apply a logical formalism to the real world entities (i.e. we can speak of it through its sign, and use logics on it through its sign).</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Object</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">SemioticObject</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The object, in Peirce semiotics, as participant to a semiotic process.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>

Sign
^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_b21a56ed_f969_4612_a6ec_cb7766f7f31d">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_b21a56ed_f969_4612_a6ec_cb7766f7f31d</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A &#x27;Sign&#x27; can have temporal-direct-parts which are &#x27;Sign&#x27; themselves.<br><br>A &#x27;Sign&#x27; usually havs &#x27;sign&#x27; spatial direct parts only up to a certain elementary semiotic level, in which the part is only a &#x27;Physical&#x27; and no more a &#x27;Sign&#x27; (i.e. it stands for nothing). This elementary semiotic level is peculiar to each particular system of signs (e.g. text, painting).<br><br>Just like an &#x27;Elementary&#x27; in the &#x27;Physical&#x27; branch, each &#x27;Sign&#x27; branch should have an a-tomistic mereological part.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">According to Peirce, &#x27;Sign&#x27; includes three subcategories:<br>- symbols: that stand for an object through convention<br>- indeces: that stand for an object due to causal continguity<br>- icons: that stand for an object due to similitudes e.g. in shape or composition</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Sign</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">An &#x27;Physical&#x27; that is used as sign (&quot;semeion&quot; in greek) that stands for another &#x27;Physical&#x27; through an semiotic process.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A novel is made of chapters, paragraphs, sentences, words and characters (in a direct parthood mereological hierarchy).<br><br>Each of them are &#x27;sign&#x27;-s.<br><br>A character can be the a-tomistic &#x27;sign&#x27; for the class of texts.<br><br>The horizontal segment in the character &quot;A&quot; is direct part of &quot;A&quot; but it is not a &#x27;sign&#x27; itself.<br><br>For plain text we can propose the ASCII symbols, for math the fundamental math symbols.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Equivalent To</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_0cd58641_824c_4851_907f_f4c3be76630c">Index</a> or <a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_35d2e130_6e01_41ed_94f7_00b333d46cf9">Conventional</a> or <a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_d7788d1a_020d_4c78_85a1_13563fcec168">Icon</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#Thing">Thing</a></td>
  </tr>

Subjective
^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_251cfb4f_5c75_4778_91ed_6c8395212fd8">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_251cfb4f_5c75_4778_91ed_6c8395212fd8</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The word subjective applies to property intrisically subjective or non-well defined. In general, when an black-box-like procedure is used for the definition of the property.<br><br>This happens due to e.g. the complexity of the object, the lack of a underlying model for the representation of the object, the non-well specified meaning of the property symbols.<br><br>A &#x27;SubjectiveProperty&#x27; cannot be used to univocally compare &#x27;Object&#x27;-s.<br><br>e.g. you cannot evaluate the beauty of a person on objective basis.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Subjective</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A coded conventional that cannot be univocally determined and depends on an agent (e.g. a human individual, a community) acting as black-box.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The beauty of that girl.<br>The style of your clothing.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>

    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#Thing">Thing</a></td>

   <div id="EMMO_4b3afb22_27cf_4ce3_88bc_492bfccb546b"></div>

Auditory
^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_4b3afb22_27cf_4ce3_88bc_492bfccb546b">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_4b3afb22_27cf_4ce3_88bc_492bfccb546b</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">&#x27;acoustical&#x27; refers to the perception mechanism of the observer that can occur through a microphone, a ear.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Altlabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Sound</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Auditory</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A &#x27;Perceptual&#x27; which stands for a real world object whose spatiotemporal pattern makes it identifiable by an observer as a sound.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">When we use the term &#x27;sound&#x27; what are we referring to? The EMMO identifis a sound as the physical object that can be heard by the observer (more exactly, by the sensor of the observer).<br><br>In this sense, a sound (which is an acoustical object) is to be identified as the air region that manifests the sound wave and is able to be perceived by an observer. In case the wave is travelling through water or steel, then these other media regions are the sounds.<br><br>If the waveform is travelling through a cable as electronic signal (analog or digital) it is no more a sound, since it cannot be perceived by an observer as an acoustical object. This electrical waveform (or digital packet) is another physical that may stand for a sound if interpreted by a device (e.g. an amplifier, a DA converter).</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#Thing">Thing</a></td>
  </tr>
  </table>

   <div id="EMMO_649bf97b_4397_4005_90d9_219755d92e34"></div>

Perceptual
^^^^^^^^^^

.. raw:: html

  <table class="element-table">
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Iri</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_649bf97b_4397_4005_90d9_219755d92e34">https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_649bf97b_4397_4005_90d9_219755d92e34</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-annotations" colspan="2">Annotations</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Comment</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">This class is the most general superclass for the categorization of contrasts that are perceivable through a specific human-related perception mechanism. This perspective is based on human characterization of perceptions.<br>A &#x27;Perceptual&#x27; can stand for another object in an EMMO described semiotic process (acting as sign or as object), just like a word on a paper (the perceptual object) may refer semiotically to another object. However, a perceptual is not necessarily a &#x27;Sign&#x27; (e.g. a line sketched on a blackboard is a recognizable &#x27;Perceptual&#x27; but it may stand for nothing).<br>A &#x27;Perceptual&#x27; becomes a semiotic object, when it is part of a &#x27;Semiotic&#x27; process described by the ontologist within the EMMO, and it&#x27;s done always specifying for which interpreter this relation occurs.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Preflabel</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">Perceptual</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Elucidation</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The class constrast individuals standing for entities that can stimulate a perception (e.g. a retina impression) to a human being and that are categorized accordingly to human perception mechanisms.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">A line scratched on a surface.<br>A sound.<br>A smell.<br>The word &#x27;cat&#x27; and the sound of the word &#x27;cat&#x27; (the first one is graphical and the second acoustical).</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Example</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value">The meta-semiotic process:<br>I see a cloud in the sky. Since I&#x27;m an EMMO ontologist, I create an individual named Cloud under the &#x27;Perceptual&#x27; class, meaning that I recognize the cloud as an object thanks to a specific perceptual channel (e.g. through my eyes). This semiotic process occurs at meta-level: it&#x27;s how I use the EMMO as tool for a direct representation of the world, understandable by others ontologists.<br><br>The semiotic process within EMMO:<br>My friend looks at the same cloud and says: &quot;It is an elephant&quot;.<br>I use the EMMO to record this experience by declaring:<br>    - my friend as MyFriend individual, belonging to &#x27;Interpreter&#x27; classes<br>    - the sound of the word &quot;elephant&quot; as an acoustical perception individual named ElephantWord, belonging to &#x27;Perceptual&#x27;<br>    - a relation hasSign between Cloud and ElephantWord, that makes ElephantWord also belonging to &#x27;Sign&#x27; class and Cloud belonging also to &#x27;Object&#x27; class<br>    - a &#x27;Semiosis&#x27; individual called MyFriendElephantCloud that hasParticipant: Cloud, ElephantWord and MyFriend, respectively as object, sign and interpreter.<br><br>So, the Perceptual class is here to categorized real-world objects at meta-level using common perceptual channels, for practical ontology usage.<br><br>We could have represented the word &quot;elephant&quot; within a physicalistic approach, by identifying it as a pressure wave in the air.</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th class="element-table-formal-description" colspan="2">Formal description</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Equivalent To</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_4b3afb22_27cf_4ce3_88bc_492bfccb546b">Auditory</a> or <a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_8f207971_aaab_48dc_a10d_55a6b4331410">Somatosensory</a> or <a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_c5ae6d8e_6b39_431f_8de4_ae4e357abc04">Visual</a> or <a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_dd14d055_2db0_4b81_bc97_ef6c2f72b8a0">Gustatory</a> or <a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_e1021593_06da_4237_8a02_29d8f6fef76d">Olfactory</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td class="element-table-key"><span class="element-table-key">Subclass Of</span></td>
    <td class="element-table-value"><a href="https://w3id.org/emmo#EMMO_1e877c70_3b01_45a8_a8f6_8ce4f6a24660">Contrast</a></td>
  </tr>
  </table>

.. raw:: html
